title: Bug Event v1
description: One append-only event in the event-sourced JSONL bug telemetry (v0.1.46 AC-1). Each line of a specs/bugs/<YYYYMMDDTHH>Z-<n>.jsonl file is one object validating this schema. A bug_id's stream opens with a `reported` event and carries at most one terminal event {resolved, superseded, deferred, rejected}; `archived` is a NON-terminal annotation (defined-but-unemitted this release).

bug_id.description: Stable identifier of the bug this event pertains to (kebab-case slug).

event.description: Event kind. `reported` opens the stream; {resolved, superseded, deferred, rejected} are terminal (at most one per bug_id); `archived` is a non-terminal annotation.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the event was recorded.

reported_by.description: Agent or runtime that recorded the event (e.g. 'software-engineer').

component.description: reported: subsystem/module the bug lives in.

context.description: reported: active spec-context the bug was found in.

symptom.description: reported: what happened (the error / wrong output).

repro.description: reported: the exact command / steps to reproduce.

notes.description: reported: environment / logs — MUST be redacted of any operator-local path, IP, hostname, private repo name, or secret.

release.description: resolved: the release that fixed the bug ('unknown' sentinel when the source did not record it).

superseded_by.description: superseded: the backlog/bug slug that supersedes this bug.

evidence.description: resolved: the resolution law's evidence (v0.1.73 FR3) — reporter-artifact reproduction + every surface the bug names. REQUIRED at the CLI append path (blocking); optional in the schema so historical pre-law events remain valid.
